note: ILLUSTRATIVE SAMPLE. Six real, well-known sources in the library schema, used to build the map until content/library.json is published. Delete this file when the curated library lands.

entries.title: Rules of Machine Learning: Best Practices for ML Engineering
entries.why: Its first rule is not to be afraid to launch without machine learning. A fair test for any AI proposal before money is committed: does the simple version already prove the need?
entries.check: Is there a heuristic baseline, and is the success metric observable and attributable before any model is trained?

entries.title: Holistic Evaluation of Language Models
entries.why: Shows how a single accuracy figure hides the trade-offs that matter, such as calibration, robustness and efficiency. Ask for that breadth before a pilot is called a success.
entries.check: Are results reported per scenario and across several metrics, on an evaluation set fixed before testing began?

entries.title: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2025
entries.why: The shared list of ways LLM applications are attacked, from prompt injection to excessive agency. A launch review that cannot answer every item is not finished.
entries.check: For each risk on the list, which control, test or monitor exists today, and who owns it?

entries.title: Hidden Technical Debt in Machine Learning Systems
entries.why: The model is a small part of a production ML system. Cost and fragility accumulate in the glue, data dependencies and feedback loops around it, which is where scaling budgets go.
entries.check: Are data dependencies, configuration and feedback loops inventoried, owned and tested like code?

entries.title: Semantic conventions for generative AI systems
entries.why: A shared vocabulary for tracing agents, model calls and tool calls, so that cost, quality and incidents can be attributed across vendors and teams.
entries.check: Do traces follow the gen_ai conventions end to end, with the convention version recorded per service?

entries.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0)
entries.why: Organises AI risk into four functions, Govern, Map, Measure and Manage, with Govern cutting across the others. A common language for boards, auditors and engineering.
entries.check: Does each production AI system have a documented owner, risk tolerance and measurement plan?
